read.title: The whole Granth, set to be read
read.body: All {angs} Angs in Sant Lipi, on warm paper or in a night scheme that is never pure black. Turn pages, jump to any Ang, pick up where you left off. Every composition opens with its printed heading.

search.title: Search the way you remember
search.body: A word in Gurmukhi, a word as it sounds in Roman letters, or just the first letters of each word — the way a line comes back to you. Auto mode works out which you meant. Verify checks a line you were sent against the text and tells you plainly.

photoBand.alt: Sri Harmandir Sahib at night, lit gold and reflected in the sarovar
photoBand.statement: Made for every day, not for scrolling.
photoBand.sub: No feed. No notifications you did not ask for. The text, and your place in it.

nitnem.title: Nitnem, with your place kept
nitnem.body: The daily banis by time of day — Japji, Jaap, Savaiye, Chaupai and Anand in the morning, Rehras at dusk, Sohila at night — with Sukhmani, Asa di Vaar and Ardaas alongside. The app remembers where you are in each and keeps a quiet record of the days you read. Reminders are optional, local, and yours to set.
nitnem.detail: Banis from Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji come from the same verified corpus, cited by Ang. Dasam Granth and Ardaas text are a separate, labelled, scholar-reviewed layer.
nitnem.ipadAlt: Nitnem on iPad in landscape: the morning banis with progress rings, and the full list by time of day
nitnem.phoneAlt: Japji Sahib open in the Nitnem reader on iPhone, cited Ang 1 to 8, at line 1 of 385

watch.title: Eight watches. {raagsWord} raags. One face.
watch.body: The day is divided into eight pahars, and different raags belong to different watches. The Raag Clock shows which belong to this one — by fixed hours, or by your local sunrise and sunset. The deep night is left in silence.
watch.alt: Raag Clock on iPhone in the dark scheme: the 2nd pahar of day and the raags sung in this watch

widgets.title: On your Home Screen and Lock Screen
widgets.body: Three widgets: the raag of the moment, the Hukam of the day with its Ang, and today's Nitnem — in sizes from small to large, with Lock Screen accessories for the raag and the Nitnem. The Hukam of the day is one complete Hukam for the whole day, chosen by the date: the same in the app and in Siri, with its opening verse on the widget. An optional Live Activity shows how far you have read a bani. It never shows a verse.
widgets.detail: Ask Siri for “Today’s Hukam”, “What raag is it now”, “Read a Vaar”, “Open a theme” or “Open a voice”. Spotlight finds your saved verses and every theme.

explore.title: Explore the Granth from every side
explore.body: An Index in the order of the saroop, with a page for every raag. All {vaars} Vaars, woven pauri by pauri as printed. {themes} themes, each with its own page. The {voices} voices of the Granth, {centuries}, each with a page of their own. Constellation, Insights and the Raag Clock beside them.

verbatim.body: The text is reproduced character for character from the source edition. Nothing is normalised, modernised or improved.
verbatim.reconciledBody: All {characters} characters are proven against the source edition, character for character — zero loss.
verbatim.sealedBody: The bundled text carries a SHA-256 checksum, fixed when the app is built.
verbatim.checkedBody: The app checks it when it is installed or updated. If a check fails, the app refuses to show the text rather than risk showing it altered.

private.body: No account. No network connections — the app works in Airplane Mode. The app has no analytics, no tracking and no third-party code. Its App Store privacy label is ‘Data Not Collected’.
private.alt: About screen on iPhone, version 1.4.9: the four scripture integrity checks, all passed
